title.en: The human eye and defects of vision

text.en: The eye works like a camera. When it fails to focus, spectacles correct it.

Light enters the eye through the cornea, then the pupil controlled by the iris, and the eye lens focuses it on the retina.
The retina has rod and cone cells that change light to electrical signals, which the optic nerve sends to the brain.
The ciliary muscles change the focal length of the lens. This is the power of accommodation. The near point is 25 cm and the far point is infinity.
Myopia (short-sightedness): distant objects look blurred because the image forms in front of the retina. It is corrected by a concave lens.
Hypermetropia (long-sightedness): near objects look blurred because the image forms behind the retina. It is corrected by a convex lens.
Presbyopia is the loss of accommodation with age and may need bifocal lenses.
Cataract is a clouding of the lens and is treated by surgery. Donating eyes after death can give sight to others.
Two eyes give a wider field of view and the ability to judge depth.

problem.en: A student cannot see the blackboard from the back row. What defect and what lens?

text.en: Distant objects look blurred, which is myopia.

why.en: The image forms before the retina.

text.en: A concave lens diverges the light before it enters the eye.
So spectacles with a concave lens are prescribed.

prompt.en: Name the parts of the eye and the common defects.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the wrong lens for correction

points.en: The retina forms the image and the optic nerve carries it to the brain.
Myopia: concave lens; hypermetropia: convex lens.
